raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

The AMD CI job `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-amd` goes red intermittently with

```
AssertionError: (0, 1, (973, 973), 'residual', nan)
```

(e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94971). The NaN comes from AITER, on
vLLM's ordinary MoE path, not from the mono kernels the test compares against.

AITER's a8w4 MoE (FP8 activations x MXFP4 weights) allocates several scratch
buffers with `torch.empty`, sized for the padded sorted length, and reads them
where the producing kernel never wrote. In FP8/E8M0 a garbage `0xFF` byte is
NaN, so a whole token row of the output comes back NaN. It only happens with a
non-zero `intermediate_pad`, at decode-sized batches, after larger calls have
run in the same process — which is why it shows up as a flaky decode failure.
Root cause, a standalone repro and a fix are filed upstream:

- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/6565
- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6568

## This change

Stop declaring `intermediate_pad` to AITER on the MXFP4 path. It is redundant
there, and dropping it keeps the call off the buggy AITER path.

Why it is redundant — the padded region is zero at the point AITER sees it, and
stays zero through every step between allocation and the kernel call:

| step | padded region | where |
|---|---|---|
| allocation | `torch.zeros` for `w13`/`w2`, their scales and `w13_bias`/`w2_bias`, at the **padded** intermediate size | `Mxfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` |
| checkpoint load | the destination is narrowed to the loaded shard before the copy, so the padded rows are never written — this is deliberate, the helper is named for it and its docstring calls out "padding ... on the shard (intermediate) dimension (e.g. for MXFP4 GEMM)" | `RoutedExperts._narrow_expert_data_for_padding`, used by `_load_w13` / `_load_w2` right before `expert_data.copy_()` |
| weight shuffle | pure `view` + `permute` (asserts `N % 16 == 0`, `K % 32 == 0`, no re-padding), so zeros stay zeros | `aiter.ops.shuffle.shuffle_weight` |
| scale shuffle | re-pads the scale to 256 rows / 8 cols, but fills the pad with `0x7F` (E8M0 = 1.0) before copying, so it is never garbage | `aiter.utility.fp4_utils.e8m0_shuffle` |

So for the padded columns the kernel computes

- stage 1: `x @ 0 = 0` (gate and up are both zero there, and the bias is zero,
  so the activation output is exactly `silu(0) * 0 = 0`)
- stage 2: `0 @ 0 = 0`

Exact zeros also mean the padded columns cannot disturb the stage-2 activation
quantization: `amax` over an MX group is unaffected by zeros, whether or not a
group straddles real and padded columns.

Two things are deliberately left alone:

- **`hidden_pad`** — the activation columns it covers are not guaranteed to be
  zero, so dropping it would not be equivalent.
- **SITU** (`activation == MoEActivation.SITU`, the a16w4 FlyDSL port used by
  Kimi K3) — that kernel consumes the pad. The surrounding code already skips
  the rounding for it ("SITU's A16W4 FlyDSL kernel pads per gate/up half; pass
  through unrounded"), and on that path AITER keys its own scratch
  initialization on the value: `_alloc = torch.zeros if inter_dim_pad > 0 else
  torch.empty` in `aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py`. Zeroing the declaration
  there would *remove* an initialization that is currently happening, which is
  the opposite of what this PR is for.

This is a workaround and should be reverted once the AITER fix is merged and
pinned. The surrounding code already carries a similar TODO about AITER padding
behaviour.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, stock AITER 0.1.25 — i.e. **without** the
AITER-side fix — running `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` unmodified,
each run covering TP2 and TP4:

| build | runs | cells | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| exactly this patch | 4 | 8 | **all passed** |
| same logic, earlier iterations of the comment/wording | 10 | 20 | **all passed** |

14 runs, 28 cells, no NaN. Before the change the same test failed intermittently
— locally about 2 runs in 6 — so 14 clean runs is about 0.3% likely if the
change did nothing.

Overhead: none measurable. Timing the same shape with and without the
declaration (median over 6 rounds, per `fused_moe_2stages` call):

| M | declared | not declared |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.139 ms | 0.141 ms |
| 4 | 0.156 ms | 0.158 ms |
| 1439 | 0.534 ms | 0.536 ms |
| 16384 | 2.010 ms | 2.010 ms |

All within run-to-run noise (~4%).

## Scope and limits

- Validated on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 (`model_dim=5120`, per-rank
  intermediate 576 padded to 640, E=384, topk=6). Other MXFP4 models on this
  path (e.g. gpt-oss with INTERLEAVE) are covered by the same zero-fill
  argument but were not run here, so reviewers may prefer a narrower gate.
- The zero-fill chain above is established from the code, with the citations in
  the table. It is not confirmed by a run against a real MXFP4 checkpoint that
  actually has padding: the test that exercises this path uses a random-weight
  loader which also zero-fills the padding, and every MXFP4 checkpoint we have
  locally has `moe_intermediate_size = 2048`, which is already aligned per rank
  (pad = 0). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (2304) is the one that pads, and the local copy
  of it is FP8 rather than MXFP4.
- Models whose per-rank intermediate size is already 128-aligned get
  `intermediate_pad == 0` and are unaffected either way.
- The `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4` opt-in is a sub-case of
  `use_mxfp4_w4a16`, so it is covered by this change as well. The same
  zero-fill argument applies to it, but it runs different kernels and was not
  exercised here.

nodes.body: Thanks for the fix! Meet the same problem when testing CI: [buildkite #95188](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95188/list?jid=01a14272-fd65-4a55-8a5b-73612cc5dc1d&tab=output).

I pushed ff92b1e56f to this branch. It keeps the DeepSeek-V4.1 NaN fix but drops the gpt-oss slowdown, and it fixes a gpt-oss TP1 accuracy bug we found while measuring.

What changed:
- The pad is now zeroed only for bias-less MXFP4 W4A16, i.e. the DeepSeek-V4.1 FlyDSL path where AITER leaves the padded columns unwritten (ROCm/aiter#6598). gpt-oss has expert biases, so it keeps declaring the pad and the CK-Tile decode kernels (`swiglu_mxfp4_bf16_cktile`, M <= 128) still skip the zero rows. Zeroing it for gpt-oss cost 6.8% throughput on gpt-oss-120b TP1.
- `aiter_moe_pads` no longer doubles the W4A16 pad at `tp_size == 1`. AITER already doubles it for the fused gate/up weight, so on main gpt-oss TP1 was told 384 rows of padding where only 192 exist, and CK-Tile skipped live rows.
- `test_aiter_mxfp4_moe_pad_masks_only_padding` now also covers the gpt-oss W4A16 layout (interleaved, biased, SWIGLUOAI). It fails on main and passes here. `test_aiter_moe_pads` covers W4A16 at TP1 and TP2.

Results on MI355X, AITER 0.1.26:

DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode numerics (`pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py`):

| | runs passed |
|---|---|
| #61960 reverted, no pad fix | 6/10 (4x `residual` NaN) |
| #61960 reverted, pad zeroed | 10/10 |
| this branch, CI command (TP2 + TP4) | 10/10 |

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash real MXFP4 checkpoint, GSM8K 5-shot at TP4: 0.906 with the pad declared vs 0.902 zeroed (within noise).

gpt-oss GPQA (`tests/evals/gpt_oss`, low effort, 8 repeats):

| | main | previous head | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b TP1 | 0.485 | 0.559 | 0.576 |
| gpt-oss-20b TP2 | 0.567 | 0.568 | unchanged from main (TP2 path not touched) |
| gpt-oss-120b TP1 | 0.648 | 0.652 | 0.667 |

gpt-oss-120b TP1 output throughput (`vllm bench serve`, random 1024/512, 3 runs each):

| concurrency | main | previous head | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 275 | 271 (-1.4%) | 271 (-1.3%) |
| 32 | 4329 | 4037 (-6.8%) | 4153 (-4.1%) |
| 128 | 9686 | 9136 (-5.7%) | 9352 (-3.5%) |

The remaining gap to main is the work main skipped incorrectly at TP1. gpt-oss-20b TP1 is within 2.4% of main at every concurrency. AITER MoE unit tests (`test_rocm_aiter_moe.py`, `test_ocp_mx_moe.py`, `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`, `-k 'aiter or Aiter or pad'`): 113 passed, 45 skipped.

The revert condition for the DeepSeek-V4.1 zeroing is now ROCm/aiter#6598, since aiter#6568 was closed. AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation and the patch; I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #97526](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97526) for commit `95fa9a08c3f7`.

ℹ️ This PR is 38 commits behind upstream `main`. Merged upstream `main` into this branch as `95fa9a08c3f7` before starting CI. Pull the branch before pushing more changes.

**Follow-up commit `3102333b12`: pre-pad `w1_bias` at load time (no more CK-Tile column-skip overhead for gpt-oss)**

After investigating why the fix still carried a 5–8 % throughput gap vs. Perry's original zeroing at M ≥ 32, I traced it to the AITER CK-Tile stage-1 kernel's `n_pad_zeros` mechanism.

**Root cause of the overhead.** The CK-Tile stage-1 kernel indexes its bias tensor with stride `kargs.N` (the full padded weight width). With `intermediate_pad = 192` the padded N is 6528 but the natural `w1_bias` is sized 6144 — a stride mismatch. The `n_pad_zeros = 384` parameter papers over this by shrinking the kernel's weight view so it only writes to the first 6144 output columns. That is correct, but it forces the kernel to branch around every tile that overlaps a padded column, costing ~6 % on the token-range CK-Tile handles (M ≤ 128).

**Fix.** Pad `w1_bias` from `[E, 6144]` to `[E, 6528]` with zeros **once at model-load time** in `GptOssMxfp4MoEMethod.get_fused_moe_quant_config`. The padded weight columns are already zero, and the padded bias entries are now zero too, so the kernel can receive `intermediate_pad = 0`, process the full output width without any masking, and write zeros for the padded columns naturally (zero weights × activation + zero bias = 0). `rocm_aiter_fused_experts` extends the existing `intermediate_pad = 0` override to cover the biased W4A16 path alongside the bias-less DSv4.1 path.

**What this does not affect.**
- DSv4.1 (bias-less): unchanged — same `intermediate_pad = 0` override, same FlyDSL path, same NaN fix as before.
- SITU: excluded from both overrides as before.
- TP2+: `aiter_moe_pads` is still called; the override zeros the result for W4A16 after the rounding/doubling step.

**Tests passed locally:** `test_aiter_moe_pads` (7/7), `test_aiter_mxfp4_moe_pad_masks_only_padding` (4/4 — SILU bias-less and SWIGLUOAI biased, both padded intermediate sizes 640 and 704).

AI assistance used (Claude Code).

✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #98815](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98815) for commit `ee3f43092275`.

ℹ️ This PR is 352 commits behind upstream `main`. Merged upstream `main` into this branch as `ee3f43092275` before starting CI. Pull the branch before pushing more changes.

✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #99316](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99316) for commit `2f21061cdb32`, running 2 failed step(s) from [Buildkite CI #98815](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98815).

merged. Please rebase the PR, @PerryZhang01.

+        ("SILU", True, False, 1, (0, 128), (0, 128)),
+        ("SILU", True, False, 2, (0, 64), (0, 64)),
+        # gpt-oss W4A16: AITER doubles the pad itself, at TP1 as at TP2.
+        ("SWIGLUOAI", False, True, 1, (0, 192), (0, 192)),
+        ("SWIGLUOAI", False, True, 2, (0, 96), (0, 64)),

     granularity, and at tp_size == 1 the intermediate pad is doubled for the
-    fused gate/up weight. The W4A4 SiLU path doubles it inside AITER, so it is
-    passed undoubled; doubling it here as well masks live intermediate rows.
+    fused gate/up weight. The W4A4 SiLU and W4A16 paths double it inside AITER,
+    so it is passed undoubled; doubling it here as well masks live
+    intermediate rows.

     - CK-Tile stage 1, aiter/fused_moe.py:
@@ -264,7 +266,11 @@ def aiter_moe_pads(
     """
     if activation == MoEActivation.SITU:

-    double = tp_size == 1 and not (use_mxfp4_w4a4 and activation == MoEActivation.SILU)
+    double = (
+        tp_size == 1
+        and not use_mxfp4_w4a16
+        and not (use_mxfp4_w4a4 and activation == MoEActivation.SILU)
+    )
     return (
         hidden_pad // 128 * 128,
         intermediate_pad // 64 * 64 * (2 if double else 1),
@@ -407,9 +413,25 @@ def rocm_aiter_fused_experts(
             intermediate_pad,
             activation,
             quant_config.use_mxfp4_w4a4,
+            quant_config.use_mxfp4_w4a16,
             moe_config.tp_size,
         )
 
+        # For W4A16 paths, declare no intermediate padding so AITER's CK-Tile
+        # stage-1 kernel processes the full weight width without the per-column
+        # skip overhead.  Two reasons this is safe:
+        #
+        # - Bias-less (DSv4.1): FlyDSL stage-1 leaves padded columns unwritten
+        #   (ROCm/aiter#6598); zero weights give zero output there.
+        # - Biased (gpt-oss): GptOssMxfp4MoEMethod.get_fused_moe_quant_config
+        #   already pre-pads w1_bias to match the padded weight width so the
+        #   CK-Tile kernel's stride-kargs.N bias access is correct.  Padded
+        #   weight columns are zero, padded bias entries are zero → zero output.
+        #
+        # SITU zeroes its own scratch on a non-zero pad so it is excluded.
+        if quant_config.use_mxfp4_w4a16 and activation != MoEActivation.SITU:
+            intermediate_pad = 0
+
         # AITER's stage1 GEMM needs gate_mode to match how weights were
         # shuffled at load time (oracle/mxfp4.py). gpt-oss uses INTERLEAVE;
         # DeepSeek V4.1 a4w4 uses SEPARATED (see below).

@@ -420,6 +420,27 @@ def get_fused_moe_quant_config(
             w1_scale = layer.w13_weight_scale
             w2_scale = layer.w2_weight_scale
 
+        # The AITER CK-Tile stage-1 kernel indexes the bias tensor with stride
+        # kargs.N (the full padded output width).  When weights are padded to a
+        # CK-Tile tile boundary the bias must be padded to match so the kernel
+        # accesses the correct per-expert row.  Pad once at load time with zeros;
+        # the padded weight columns are also zero so those output positions end up
+        # as zero without any in-kernel masking.  The forward pass can then pass
+        # intermediate_pad=0 for the biased path, eliminating the column-skip
+        # overhead in the CK-Tile kernel (see rocm_aiter_moe.py).
+        if (
+            w1_bias is not None
+            and self.moe.intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded is not None
+        ):
+            inter_pad = (
+                self.moe.intermediate_size_per_partition
+                - self.moe.intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded
+            )

+                )
+

             mxfp4_backend=self.mxfp4_backend,
             w1_scale=w1_scale,

issue_comments.body: Thanks for the fix! Meet the same problem when testing CI: [buildkite #95188](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95188/list?jid=01a14272-fd65-4a55-8a5b-73612cc5dc1d&tab=output).

I pushed ff92b1e56f to this branch. It keeps the DeepSeek-V4.1 NaN fix but drops the gpt-oss slowdown, and it fixes a gpt-oss TP1 accuracy bug we found while measuring.

What changed:
- The pad is now zeroed only for bias-less MXFP4 W4A16, i.e. the DeepSeek-V4.1 FlyDSL path where AITER leaves the padded columns unwritten (ROCm/aiter#6598). gpt-oss has expert biases, so it keeps declaring the pad and the CK-Tile decode kernels (`swiglu_mxfp4_bf16_cktile`, M <= 128) still skip the zero rows. Zeroing it for gpt-oss cost 6.8% throughput on gpt-oss-120b TP1.
- `aiter_moe_pads` no longer doubles the W4A16 pad at `tp_size == 1`. AITER already doubles it for the fused gate/up weight, so on main gpt-oss TP1 was told 384 rows of padding where only 192 exist, and CK-Tile skipped live rows.
- `test_aiter_mxfp4_moe_pad_masks_only_padding` now also covers the gpt-oss W4A16 layout (interleaved, biased, SWIGLUOAI). It fails on main and passes here. `test_aiter_moe_pads` covers W4A16 at TP1 and TP2.

Results on MI355X, AITER 0.1.26:

DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode numerics (`pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py`):

| | runs passed |
|---|---|
| #61960 reverted, no pad fix | 6/10 (4x `residual` NaN) |
| #61960 reverted, pad zeroed | 10/10 |
| this branch, CI command (TP2 + TP4) | 10/10 |

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash real MXFP4 checkpoint, GSM8K 5-shot at TP4: 0.906 with the pad declared vs 0.902 zeroed (within noise).

gpt-oss GPQA (`tests/evals/gpt_oss`, low effort, 8 repeats):

| | main | previous head | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b TP1 | 0.485 | 0.559 | 0.576 |
| gpt-oss-20b TP2 | 0.567 | 0.568 | unchanged from main (TP2 path not touched) |
| gpt-oss-120b TP1 | 0.648 | 0.652 | 0.667 |

gpt-oss-120b TP1 output throughput (`vllm bench serve`, random 1024/512, 3 runs each):

| concurrency | main | previous head | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 275 | 271 (-1.4%) | 271 (-1.3%) |
| 32 | 4329 | 4037 (-6.8%) | 4153 (-4.1%) |
| 128 | 9686 | 9136 (-5.7%) | 9352 (-3.5%) |

The remaining gap to main is the work main skipped incorrectly at TP1. gpt-oss-20b TP1 is within 2.4% of main at every concurrency. AITER MoE unit tests (`test_rocm_aiter_moe.py`, `test_ocp_mx_moe.py`, `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`, `-k 'aiter or Aiter or pad'`): 113 passed, 45 skipped.

The revert condition for the DeepSeek-V4.1 zeroing is now ROCm/aiter#6598, since aiter#6568 was closed. AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation and the patch; I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #97526](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97526) for commit `95fa9a08c3f7`.

ℹ️ This PR is 38 commits behind upstream `main`. Merged upstream `main` into this branch as `95fa9a08c3f7` before starting CI. Pull the branch before pushing more changes.

**Follow-up commit `3102333b12`: pre-pad `w1_bias` at load time (no more CK-Tile column-skip overhead for gpt-oss)**

After investigating why the fix still carried a 5–8 % throughput gap vs. Perry's original zeroing at M ≥ 32, I traced it to the AITER CK-Tile stage-1 kernel's `n_pad_zeros` mechanism.

**Root cause of the overhead.** The CK-Tile stage-1 kernel indexes its bias tensor with stride `kargs.N` (the full padded weight width). With `intermediate_pad = 192` the padded N is 6528 but the natural `w1_bias` is sized 6144 — a stride mismatch. The `n_pad_zeros = 384` parameter papers over this by shrinking the kernel's weight view so it only writes to the first 6144 output columns. That is correct, but it forces the kernel to branch around every tile that overlaps a padded column, costing ~6 % on the token-range CK-Tile handles (M ≤ 128).

**Fix.** Pad `w1_bias` from `[E, 6144]` to `[E, 6528]` with zeros **once at model-load time** in `GptOssMxfp4MoEMethod.get_fused_moe_quant_config`. The padded weight columns are already zero, and the padded bias entries are now zero too, so the kernel can receive `intermediate_pad = 0`, process the full output width without any masking, and write zeros for the padded columns naturally (zero weights × activation + zero bias = 0). `rocm_aiter_fused_experts` extends the existing `intermediate_pad = 0` override to cover the biased W4A16 path alongside the bias-less DSv4.1 path.

**What this does not affect.**
- DSv4.1 (bias-less): unchanged — same `intermediate_pad = 0` override, same FlyDSL path, same NaN fix as before.
- SITU: excluded from both overrides as before.
- TP2+: `aiter_moe_pads` is still called; the override zeros the result for W4A16 after the rounding/doubling step.

**Tests passed locally:** `test_aiter_moe_pads` (7/7), `test_aiter_mxfp4_moe_pad_masks_only_padding` (4/4 — SILU bias-less and SWIGLUOAI biased, both padded intermediate sizes 640 and 704).
